reading.title: The Porch Science Club
reading.purpose: Watch two siblings test forces, light, and sound using everyday objects on their porch.
paras: On Saturday afternoon, Kofi and his sister Zara turned their back porch into a science lab. Their goal was to build a toy racer powered by a spring.

Kofi pushed a metal spring down to compress it, squeezing it into a tiny space behind the car. "Hold on," Zara said. "When you release it, letting go all at once, the spring will propel the car forward across the boards."

Kofi let go, and the racer zoomed ahead! Halfway across the porch, it rolled onto a rough doormat and slowed down. "That is friction," Zara noted, pointing to the bumpy fibers rubbing against the wheels. At the porch edge, the car tipped off, and gravity pulled it straight down onto the soft grass.

Next, they tested light and sound. Zara angled a pocket mirror to reflect sunlight onto the shed wall, bouncing the beam right across the yard. When Kofi tossed a foam ball at a tilted cardboard shield, the shield managed to deflect the ball sideways. Then Zara tapped an empty tin can and felt its sides vibrate, shaking back and forth so fast they hummed.

"Time for cocoa!" their dad called from the kitchen, clicking the stove dial to ignite the burner. Zara grinned. Even resisting the cold wind outside could not stop them from testing one more launch, though the icy breeze tried to resist every step they took indoors.

choices: to let go of a spring so it jumps forward
to press something into a smaller space
to bounce a beam of sunlight off a mirror
to shake back and forth until a can hums
qs.why: Paragraph 2 says Kofi pushed the spring down to compress it, "squeezing it into a tiny space."

qs.q: Which sentence shows what caused the toy racer to slow down?
choices: Kofi let go, and the racer zoomed ahead!
"That is friction," Zara noted, pointing to the bumpy fibers rubbing against the wheels.
At the porch edge, the car tipped off, and gravity pulled it straight down onto the soft grass.
Next, they tested light and sound.
qs.why: This sentence explains that friction from the doormat's bumpy fibers rubbing the wheels slowed the car.

ev.text: "That is friction," Zara noted, pointing to the bumpy fibers rubbing against the wheels.

qs.q: Why did the tin can hum when Zara tapped it?
choices: Its metal sides shook back and forth very quickly.
Sunlight bounced off the pocket mirror and heated the tin can.
The cardboard shield pushed the tin can sideways across the porch.
The icy wind blew through the kitchen door and shook the table.
qs.why: Paragraph 4 says the sides of the tin can vibrated, shaking back and forth so fast they hummed.

qs.q: What is this story mostly about?
choices: How to cook hot cocoa safely on a kitchen stove on a cold winter night
Why rough doormats should be kept off wooden back porches
Two siblings testing forces, light, and sound on a porch
How to build a cardboard shield to block sunlight in a yard
qs.why: Kofi and Zara test a spring racer, friction, gravity, mirrors, shields, and sound on their porch.

clues.text: squeezing it into a tiny space
bouncing the beam right across the yard
shaking back and forth so fast they hummed

reading.retellFrame: On the porch, Kofi and Zara learned that ___ makes the racer move while ___ slows it down.
